finding.claim: Schema $ref resolution reads local files outside the input directory. Under the default allow_remote_refs=None only a deprecation warning is emitted, and --url forces allow_remote_refs=True, so a fetched remote schema can read arbitrary local files that parse as a JSON/YAML mapping and embed their contents in generated output or error messages.
finding.source: $ref values inside the schema document (file:// URIs or relative paths containing ../), supplied by whoever authors the schema, including a remote schema fetched via --url (src/datamodel_code_generator/__main__.py:2970-2971).
finding.sink: load_data_from_path / path.read_bytes on the resolved local path (parser/jsonschema.py:11002-11005, reached from _get_ref_body_from_url :11071-11085 and _get_ref_body_from_remote :11098-11106).

trace.note: --url with allow_remote_refs None forces allow_remote_refs = True
_get_ref_body: file:// is_url routed to _get_ref_body_from_url; only allow_remote_refs is False blocks, warning only for http(s)
_get_ref_body_from_url: file:// branch takes the path from the ref via url2pathname
_resolve_local_ref_path resolves the path before the base-path check
allowed when inside base_path or allow_remote_refs is True
allow_remote_refs None: warn_deprecated and return outside path (allowed)
_get_ref_body_from_remote: relative refs joined to base_path go through the same check (../ escapes allowed by default)
file parsed as JSON/YAML mapping and used as a schema; parse and not-found errors echo the path (:11108)

finding.guards_checked: Symlink and .. handled by resolve() before the check (correct). Base-path containment enforced only when allow_remote_refs is True or inside base_path. Default None warns but allows. Only allow_remote_refs False blocks. No origin check on the referring document. Content must parse as a dict, which limits what can be extracted. Exfiltration requires the output or logs to be visible to the attacker.
